correctness.rationale: For every n>=1 and 0<t<1 the conditional iid-uniform law gives exact empirical-count squared bias and variance, which integrate to the stated closed form. The distinct beta-order-statistic log representation yields an everywhere positive second derivative and divergent endpoints. Beta log-covariances derived from conditioned order statistics give the exact harmonic mixed moment, including n=1, strict negative sign for n>=2 and harmonic asymptotic. An embedded finite checker passed 100 conditional identities, 500 rational mixed-moment cases and 12 seeded conditional simulation cases; the all-size proof does not depend on finite numerics.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparisons found no largest-order-statistic conditional regression or finite-sample mixed covariance; the nearest article on parametric conditional laws explicitly excludes Anderson–Darling. Semantically and algebraically, the new maximum-specific joint moment is not a corollary of the prior marginal AD distribution or of cross-EDF covariances. An unindexed classical joint order-statistic identity remains a genuine residual risk, so no universal historical-uniqueness claim is made.
residual_risks: A classical exact joint distribution of the full Anderson–Darling statistic with an extreme uniform order statistic might encode the same finite-n mixed moment, but was not located.
The original Anderson–Darling 1954 paper was consulted for historical attribution through its abstract only; no whole-text no-coverage conclusion is drawn from that source.

value.rationale: The maximum is the canonical upper-tail observation, and Anderson–Darling weights empirical discrepancies at both tails. Exact conditional expectation for all interior maxima proves a unique mean-loss minimizer and blowup at both extremes; the exactly negative aggregate covariance distinguishes local nonlinear dependence from its global first moment. This natural calibration-related structural fact is not a parameter renaming, arbitrary slice or known marginal-table recomputation.
